info.title: FCP admin API
info.description: The Ferrous Communications Platform admin API. Every request carries `Authorization: Bearer <token>`: the static token, a session from `/auth/login`, or an API token (`docs/API_TOKENS.md`). Errors are `{error, code, details}`, times are RFC 3339, and lists are `{data, next_cursor, total}` paged by `limit` and `cursor`.

get.summary: GET /provisioning/:mac_address -- Auto-provision a phone by MAC address.
get.description:
Phones must present both:
- `Authorization: Bearer <token>`
- or `X-FCP-Provisioning-Token: <token>`
- and `X-FCP-Device-Provisioning-Token: <per-device-token>`

Unknown or unauthorized devices all return the same 404 to avoid turning
this endpoint into an enumeration surface.

Example: ws://localhost:8080/api/v1/events?event_types=call&tenant_id=123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000

delete.summary:
Delete a tenant (platform admin only). A request, not a statement
(`docs/COMPLIANCE_FOLLOWUPS.md` §4): refused with `409` while a legal
hold is active; otherwise the tenant is closed and `202` returns the
tenant deletion request, which `fcp-admin` runs — every row of the
tenant removed, the tenant last. Its progress is at
`/compliance/subject-requests/:id` in the tenant.

post.description:
POST /api/v1/users

**Security Note**: This endpoint uses constant-time operations to prevent
user enumeration attacks. Even if a user exists, we perform password hashing
before returning an error to match the timing of successful creation.

POST /api/v1/users/:username/unlock

Resets failed login attempts, clears lockout, and sets account status to Active.

put.summary: Update digest password (Cisco-style separate SIP credentials).
put.description:
PUT /api/v1/users/:username/digest-password

This sets a separate password for SIP authentication, providing security isolation
between API/web access and SIP phone registration (Cisco CUCM style).

**Security Benefits:**
- Compromised SIP credentials don't expose API/admin access
- Different password policies for phones vs admin users
- Separate rotation schedules for SIP and API credentials

**Note:** If digest_password is not set (NULL), the main password is used for SIP.

delete.summary: Delete digest password (revert to using main password for SIP).
delete.description:
DELETE /api/v1/users/:username/digest-password

Removes the separate digest password and reverts to using the main password
for SIP authentication. The HA1 hash will be recomputed from the main password.

`GET /compliance/subject-requests/:id/bundle`: the export's bundle, a

`POST /compliance/subject-requests/:id/confirm`: confirm an erasure's
preview. The erasure then runs against the data as it is, not as the
preview found it, and cannot be undone. `409` unless a preview is waiting.

ApiTokenResponse.description: Response model for an API token (never includes a hash).

scope.description:
`admin` (the admin API under its permissions) or `personal` (its
maker's own `/me` routes).

created_by.description:
The maker's username; empty for a token made with the static token or
before makers were recorded.

legacy_full_access.description:
A token made before permissions were checked, carrying `admin` or
`*`: it reaches everything in its tenant. Review and replace it.

previous_secret_valid_until.description: Until when the secret a rotation replaced still opens the token.

available.description: Funds that may still be spent (balance + credit limit).

oneOf.description: The tenant's prepaid/credit balance, when one is configured.

CallerIdPolicy.description: How a user's caller ID leaves on a trunk.

CallingResponse.description:
The settings as the API shows them: targets in their string form
(`voicemail`, `number:+15551234567`, `ext:2001`, `user:<id>`, a SIP URI).

hold_music.description: A prompt's id, `none` for silence, or absent for the tenant's music.

after_hours_schedule_id.description: The user's hours and where calls go outside them (§3.5).

oneOf.description:
Find-me / follow-me (§3.6): `enabled`, and `steps` of `targets`
(`devices`, `ext:…`, `number:+…`, `user:…`, a SIP URI), `ring_secs`
and `confirm`.

class_of_service_id.description: The user's class of service (§3.7); `None` is the tenant's default.

oneOf.description:
The user as an executive (§3.10): `enabled`, `filter` (`all`,
`external`, `none`), `alert` (`assistants`,
`assistants_and_executive`), and `assistants` (`user_id`,
`opted_in`) in order.

kind.description: What the record is a record of: `call`, `queue`, `conference`, `gateway`.

direction.description:
`inbound`, `outbound` or `internal` once the pipeline has enriched
the record; absent until then.

trunk_id.description:
Which trunk carried the call (`docs/TENANT_TRUNKS.md` §4): two
tenants may both have a "carrier-a".

recording_consent.description:
`announced`, `failed`, `not_required` or `refused` when the call was
to be recorded; absent otherwise.

CivicElements.description:
The RFC 5139 civic address elements beyond city, state, postal code and
country, which [`E911Address`] carries as fields of its own.

house_number.description: `HNO`: the numeric part of the house number (`1455`).

name.description: `NAM`: the name of the place (`Example HQ`).

ClassOfServiceRequest.description:
What a class is written as. `allowed` unset allows everything;
`max_calls` unset is two, `null` no limit.

ClassReport.description: What one class of data gave up to an export.

files.description: Media files put in the bundle.

missing_files.description:
Media files that are the subject's but could not be read from this
host, with why.

held.description: Items under a legal hold (exported like the rest).

ClusterNodeInfo.description: Information about a single cluster node, enriched with derived fields.

started_at.description:
When the node started, as RFC 3339 in the admin API
(`docs/DEVELOPER_SURFACE.md` §3, phase 2b); epoch seconds here.

region.description: Deployment region the node advertises, when it has one.

video_budget.description: Video budget per device, when the node advertises one.

oneOf.description:
What the node will carry and what it is carrying, when it keeps
limits (`docs/CAPACITY_AND_SURVIVABILITY.md` §7).

calls_left.description: Calls this node will still take, when it says what it allows.

oneOf.description:
The node's own view of the cluster, when it does not look whole
(`docs/MULTI_REGION_FOLLOWUPS.md` §2.3).

ClusterNodeStatus.description: Status of a cluster node, derived from its Redis key TTL.

ClusterSitesResponse.description:
Response for GET /api/v1/cluster/sites: every tenant's sites, as the
tenant API shows one.

ClusterStats.description: Aggregate statistics across all cluster nodes.

nodes_by_region.description: Nodes per advertised region; nodes without one are not counted here.

nodes_with_partial_view.description:
Nodes whose own view of the cluster does not look whole — most
often every node of a region that has lost the others (§2.3).

version_skew.description:
More than one release is running: an upgrade under way, or one
that stopped half way.

ClusterView.description:
This node's view, as `/status`, the heartbeat record and the
`system.cluster_view_changed` event carry it.

since.description: When the current state began (Unix seconds); absent while whole.

lost_regions.description: The regions whose every node went at once.

view_age_secs.description:
Seconds since discovery last worked — how old the member list is.
Absent before the first discovery.

database_reachable.description:
Whether the node reaches its database, when it has a probe and the
view is not whole.

value.description: A configuration section: a JSON object.

ContactInput.description:
A contact on the way in: either the plain string the API took before
block 2, read by its shape, or a typed object.

ContactReadiness.description:
One contact and how it has fared (§8.4): a tenant should be able to
see that its notifications work before it needs them to.

issues.description: What keeps this contact from being delivered to.

last_delivery_at.description: When anything was last delivered to it.

last_test_at.description: When a `933` test call's notice last reached it.

ContactResponse.description: One notification contact as the API shows it.

issues.description: What keeps this contact from being delivered to, empty when it can.

CreateApiTokenRequest.description: Request body for creating a new admin API token.

permissions.description:
Permission names (`Permission::as_str`), or `admin` for everything
the maker may grant.

CreateApiTokenResponse.description: Response body after creating a token (includes the one-time secret).

sip_username.description: Credentials of the device's own (§3.8): both, or neither.

hoteling_host.description: A shared phone users may log in on.

provisioning_token.description:
Optional per-device provisioning token. If omitted for a device with a
MAC address, a token is generated and returned once in the create response.

schedule_id.description: A schedule of the tenant; empty clears it.

closed_target.description:
A call target (`voicemail`, `number:+…`, `ext:…`, `flow:…`,
`queue:…`, a SIP URI); empty clears it.

shared.description: A shared line: its devices share its appearances (§3.9).

max_appearances.description: How many calls a shared line carries at once (1 to 24).

barge_in.description: A phone on the shared line may barge into an active appearance.

cidr.description: A range (`10.1.2.0/24`) or a single address.

location_id.description: The site an address on this network is at.

CreatePersonalTokenRequest.description: Request body for creating a personal API token.

site_id.description: The site whose phones answer this number; empty to answer it here.

schedule_id.description: A schedule of the tenant; empty clears it.

closed_target.description: A call target; empty clears it.

CreateTenantRequest.description: Request to create a new tenant

sip_domains.description: SIP domains to claim on behalf of the new tenant.

platform_trunk_fallback.description:
Whether the platform's trunks may carry this tenant's calls when it
has none of its own that can (`docs/TENANT_TRUNKS.md` §5). True
unless said otherwise.

oneOf.description: How the tenant dials and keeps time.

kind.description:
`top_up` (positive amount) or `adjustment` (either sign).
`call_charge` entries are written only by settlement.

currency.description:
Currency used when this entry creates the tenant's balance row.
Defaults to USD.

external_ref.description:
Reference to the external billing system's record (invoice id,
payment id, ...).

site_id.description: The site this trunk runs at; empty to make it the cloud's own.

sip_provisioning_password.description:
Optional SIP password retained for device auto-provisioning templates.

When set, this becomes the user's SIP digest password and is exposed by
provisioning as `${sip_password}` for vendors that cannot use HA1.

DataClass.description: The classes of data a hold can cover.

reached.description: Whether this host reached the dead letters.

allOf.description: RFC 5139 civic elements, as `/v1/locations` takes them.

DeclaredLocationResponse.description: A user's declared location: where they are when no network places them.

current.description: False once it has expired: the platform stops using it.

DestinationClass.description: What kind of destination a dialled number is.

DestinationOverride.description:
A tenant's own word on a range of numbers: `prefix` is E.164 when it
starts with `+` (`+1900`), or the digits as dialled otherwise (`118`).
The longest matching override wins over the built-in table.

sip_username.description:
The username of the device's own credentials; the password and its
hash are never returned (`docs/ENTERPRISE_CALLING.md` §3.8).

hoteling_host.description: A shared phone users may log in on.

e911_trust_location.description:
Whether this device is trusted to send its own location with a
call (`docs/E911_BLOCK_2.md` §6.3); `null` follows its type.

allOf.description:
RFC 5139 civic elements (`house_number`, `street_name`,
`street_suffix`, `unit`, …), beside the lines above
(`docs/E911_BLOCK_2.md` §5.1).

validated.description:
Whether a validator has confirmed this address. Read-only: an

PresenceAuthPolicy.description:
Authorization policy for presence subscriptions.

Determines which watchers are allowed to subscribe to a presentity's state.
If no policy is set for a presentity, all watchers are allowed (default open).

Evaluation order (first match wins):
1. Block list (AOR exact match) → deny
2. Per-event block list → deny
3. Block patterns (domain wildcard) → deny
4. Allow list (AOR exact match) → allow
5. Per-event allow list → allow (if non-empty, restricts to listed AORs)
6. Allow patterns (domain wildcard) → allow
7. Time window check → deny if outside windows
8. Default

default_allow.description:

watchers on the allow_list are permitted.

block_list.description: Watcher AORs explicitly blocked from subscribing.

event_allow.description:
Event-package-specific allow lists. Key: event package name.
If a watcher's event package has an entry here, only listed AORs
may subscribe for that specific package.

time_windows.description:
Optional time windows during which subscriptions are allowed.
Empty = always allowed.

allow_patterns.description: Group-based allow patterns. Supports domain wildcards like `*@domain`.

country.description:
ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 (`US`, `GB`, …), for classifying the numbers the
tenant's users dial; unset reads numbers as North American.

timezone.description: IANA timezone, the default for the tenant's new schedules.

destination_overrides.description:
The tenant's own classification of number ranges, over the
built-in table.

hoteling_session_hours.description:
How long a hoteling guest stays logged in on a host phone
(`docs/ENTERPRISE_CALLING.md` §3.8); unset is
[`crate::hoteling::DEFAULT_SESSION_HOURS`].

TenantId.description: A TenantId: `tenant-<uuid>`, or the bare UUID

sip_domains.description: SIP domains claimed by this tenant. See `Tenant::sip_domains`.

platform_trunk_fallback.description:
Whether this tenant's calls may leave on the platform's trunks when
it has none of its own that can take them (`docs/TENANT_TRUNKS.md`).

TimeWindow.description: A time window during which subscriptions are allowed.

end_hour.description: End hour (0-23, UTC). If end < start, wraps past midnight.

days.description: Days of week (0=Sun, 1=Mon, ..., 6=Sat). Empty = all days.

TrunkNodeView.description: What one node sees of one trunk.

node_id.description:
The node this is the view of. Absent inside a node's own report,
which names its node once; set where views of one trunk from many
nodes are gathered, as `/v1/trunks` does.

tenant_id.description: The platform's own trunks have no tenant.

health.description:
`healthy`, `degraded`, `down` or `unknown` — what this node's own
probes have found, not what another node found.

hosts_down.description:
Hosts of the trunk this node's last probe found down; a call tries
them after the ones that answered (`docs/DEPLOYMENT_GAPS.md` §1.8).

calls_in_flight.description:
Calls this node has on the trunk right now. Capacity is per node
(§13.3), so this is a share of the carrier's channels, not all of
them.

routable.description:
Whether this node would route a call to the trunk now: enabled,
not administratively disabled and not down.

registration.description:
For a registering trunk, what this node's binding is doing:
`registered`, `pending`, `failed` or `unregistered`. Absent on a
trunk that does not register, and `unregistered` on one another
node holds.

account.description: The carrier account bound, when the trunk registers as itself.

site_id.description:
The site this trunk runs at, in a hybrid deployment
(`docs/HYBRID_CONTROL_PLANE.md` §3.6); absent for the cloud's own.

link.description:
`cloud` or `site`: which end of a site's link this trunk is, when
it is one. Made at enrollment, never set through this API.

nodes.description:
What each node that routes by this trunk sees of it
(`docs/TENANT_TRUNKS.md` §9): a carrier one node cannot reach may
be reachable from another, and that disagreement is worth showing.
Empty where no node publishes a view.

calls_in_flight.description: Calls on this trunk across every node that reported one.

routable_somewhere.description: Whether any node would route a call to it now.

TrunkStats.description: Aggregated statistics for a trunk computed from CDRs.

acd_secs.description: Average Call Duration in seconds (answered calls only)

hourly_volume.description: Call volume per hour for last 24h (24 buckets, oldest first)

UpdateBalanceRequest.description:
Balance settings update. Every field is optional; the balance amount
itself is only changed through transactions.

low_balance_threshold.description: `null` clears the threshold; omit to leave it unchanged.

UpdateCallingRequest.description:
What may change. A forward given as an empty string is cleared; one
left out is kept. A ring time of `0` clears it (the node's default).

hold_music.description:
A prompt of the tenant, `none`, or an empty string for the
tenant's hold music.

after_hours_schedule_id.description: A schedule of the tenant, or an empty string to clear it.

after_hours_forward.description: A call target, or an empty string to clear it.

oneOf.description: Replaces the find-me whole when given.

class_of_service_id.description:
A class of service of the tenant, or an empty string for the
tenant's default. An admin's to set: refused at `/me/calling`.

oneOf.description: The user as an executive (§3.10); each field kept when left out.

value.description: A configuration section: a JSON object.

owner_user_id.description: `null` (or an empty string) leaves the device without an owner.

sip_username.description:
The username of the device's own credentials; `null` removes them.
A new username needs `sip_password` too, since the digest hash is
made from both.

oneOf.description:
The address for this phone alone. `null` removes it, so a phone
that goes back to its site stops carrying where it used to be
(`docs/E911.md`).

e911_trust_location.description:
Trust this device's own location (`docs/E911_BLOCK_2.md` §6.3).
`null` returns it to whatever the tenant trusts its device type with.

provisioning_token.description: Set or rotate the per-device provisioning token. An empty string clears it.

UpdateDigestPasswordRequest.description: Update digest password request (for Cisco-style separate SIP credentials).

store_for_provisioning.description:
Retain the plaintext SIP password for auto-provisioning templates.

Defaults to true because most desk-phone provisioning templates require
a raw SIP password rather than HA1/precomputed digest material.

contacts.description: Replaces the notification contacts. Strings are read by shape.

notify_contacts.description:
The field this took before block 2; `contacts` wins when both are
given.

trust_device_locations.description:
Device types trusted to send their own location (`softphone`,
`desk_phone`, `webrtc`, `mobile`, …); replaces the list.

declared_location_ttl_secs.description: How long a declared location stands, in seconds (60 to 30 days).

schedule_id.description: A schedule of the tenant; empty clears it.

closed_target.description:
A call target (`voicemail`, `number:+…`, `ext:…`, `flow:…`,
`queue:…`, a SIP URI); empty clears it.

shared.description: A shared line: its devices share its appearances (§3.9).

max_appearances.description: How many calls a shared line carries at once (1 to 24).

barge_in.description: A phone on the shared line may barge into an active appearance.

oneOf.description: Replaces the civic elements when given.

retention_days.description: Double Option: outer = field not provided, inner = null to clear.

UpdateMeetingRequest.description: Update meeting request body (all fields optional).

UpdateMyExecutive.description: What an assistant changes of their own part in an executive's handling.

site_id.description: The site whose phones answer this number; empty to answer it here.

UpdatePolicyRequest.description: Every field optional; `null` on a retention field means "keep forever".

schedule_id.description: A schedule of the tenant; empty clears it.

closed_target.description: A call target; empty clears it.

sip_domains.description:
Full replacement for the tenant's SIP domain list. Use `None` to
leave the list alone; use `Some(vec![])` to clear it.

platform_trunk_fallback.description: Whether the platform's trunks may carry this tenant's calls.

oneOf.description: Replaces the tenant's calling defaults whole when given.

UpsertRateRequest.description: Create or replace a rate on a plan.

total_cost.description:
Sum of rated call costs in the period, in the tenant's rate-plan
currency (0 when billing is not configured).

UserId.description: A UserId: `user-<uuid>`, or the bare UUID

nomadic.description:
Whether every device of this user's moves (a softphone, a mobile or
a browser), so where it was provisioned may not be where it is.

issues.description: Why the user is not (fully) ready; empty when ready.

notes.description:
What the validator could not do on an otherwise good address: the
parts of the street it could not tell apart, say.

provider_reference.description: The provider's reference for this answer, when it gave one.

VideoCodec.description:
Video codecs FCP negotiates (the five forge-media carries; see
`docs/VIDEO_CONFERENCING.md` §6). Every one uses the 90 kHz RTP clock
and a dynamic payload type that comes from the offer, so there is no
fixed payload type here: the old fixed numbers put VP9 on 101, the
telephone-event type.

VideoDeviceBudget.description:
One device's video budget on a node, in work units: one unit is a
thousandth of one execution unit's time per second (on the host, a
millicore of one codec-pool thread). `left` is what a new room or
participant may still cost here.

codecs.description: SDP names of the codecs the device *encodes* (`H264`, `VP8`, …).

left.description:
What a new room or participant may still cost here: on a device
with engines, the tightest engine's.

oneOf.description:
A GPU's engines, each a budget of its own (FCP §15.8): NVENC,
NVDEC and the compute cores saturate separately, and placement
wants the encoder's. Absent on the host, and on a node from
before engines were advertised.

VideoEngines.description: The three budgets of a GPU.

ViewState.description: What this node's view of the cluster looks like.

WeeklyWindow.description:
A span of hours on some days: `start` to `end` local time; an `end`
before its `start` runs past midnight into the next day, and an `end`
equal to its `start` is the whole day.

client_address.description: The address the caller was seen at, when one placed them.

declared_age_secs.description: For a declared location, how long ago the user declared it.

me.MailboxResponse.description: Mailbox response (reuse same shape as admin).

recording_id.description: The recording's id, when one started.

consent.description: What the parties were told: `announced`, `failed` or `not_required`.

consent_announced.description: True when a recording-consent announcement was played first.

bearer.description: The static token, a session JWT, or an `fcp_…` API token
